Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The test `testNodeSetOperations` fails on the expression "$array > 0". According to the current bug report, the issue is related to the incorrect behavior of binary operators when involving node-sets, specifically the ">" comparison in XPath. The XPath specification states that when comparing a node-set to a number, the comparison should be true if there is any node in the node-set whose string value, converted to a number, satisfies the comparison. Similarly, for node-set comparisons, it involves checking all node pairs.

The test tries to evaluate this behavior using an XPath expression, expecting the result `Boolean.TRUE`. However, this behavior is not correctly implemented, likely in the evaluation logic of binary operations involving node-set operands.

The CoreOperation class is a probable location where operations are handled. Unfortunately, direct code snippets for critical methods handling node-set binary operations (e.g., evaluate or evaluateNodeSetComparison) were not found. No recent relevant defect reports explicitly describe a similar binary operation issue except the current one, which indicates this problem is isolated.

The root cause of the failure is that the comparison operation between node-sets and numbers (or between two node-sets) is not implemented according to the XPath specification. The implementation likely compares entire node-sets as objects or incorrectly handles conversion/scalar expansion, thus failing the test that expects a boolean comparison result based on any-node match.

In conclusion, the bug occurs due to incorrect handling of comparison operators involving node-sets during evaluation in `CoreOperation` or a related class responsible for XPath expression evaluation of binary operators. The test fails because the XPath expression comparison involving node-sets does not faithfully implement the XPath spec's semantics for such comparisons.

Next, the most relevant method to fix would be the one in `CoreOperation` or related classes that evaluate binary operator expressions involving node-sets, ensuring the logic matches the XPath spec for node-set comparisons.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
